system.name: Mugi
system.one_liner: a value-level-parallelism (VLP) accelerator that replaces multipliers and lookup tables with temporal spike-coded comparators and shared accumulators/LUT rows for efficient LLM inference

content.subject: how a floating-point LUT lookup for exp() is split into row (mantissa) and element (exponent) temporal subscriptions

elements.name: LUT
elements.role: lookup table storing precomputed exp() values, addressed to retrieve a value or a row of values

elements.name: Addr
elements.role: the address fed into the LUT to select an entry or row

elements.name: Val
elements.role: the LUT's output: a single value in the naive scheme, or a row of values in the split scheme

elements.name: LUT row
elements.role: a row of consecutive exp() values fetched together for one shared sign-mantissa address (S-M)

elements.name: i: S-M
elements.role: the sign+mantissa fields of the floating-point input, used to address which LUT row to fetch

elements.name: i: E
elements.role: the exponent field of the floating-point input, used to select one element within the fetched row

elements.name: TC
elements.role: Temporal Converter that emits a spike to subscribe to either the LUT row (mantissa TC) or one row element (exponent TC)

elements.name: exp
elements.role: the final selected output value exp(S-M-E) captured for one input

elements.name: Cycle
elements.role: the clock-cycle axis along which LUT rows become available and subscriptions fire

relations.what: an address selects an entry (naive scheme) or a row (split scheme) from the LUT
the LUT outputs the addressed value or row
the mantissa/sign field drives a TC that subscribes to the matching LUT row
the mantissa TC's spike selects/captures the row of values matching S-M
a second TC keyed on the exponent field subscribes to one element of the LUT row
the exponent subscription selects one element of the row as the final exp(S-M-E) output

panels.label: (a) naive LUT
panels.differs: baseline: one address i directly indexes one LUT entry, returning exp(i) in one step

panels.label: (b) sequential bottleneck
panels.differs: the naive LUT can serve only one input per access; concurrent lookups for i[1], i[k] are blocked (red X)

panels.label: (c) two-step split
panels.differs: splits the lookup into fetching a row of consecutive values first, then selecting one value from that row

panels.label: (d) floating-point row addressing
panels.differs: applies the two-step split to a floating-point input: sign-mantissa (S-M) addresses a row of the LUT laid out as exp(S-M-E)

panels.label: (e) row element selection
panels.differs: the exponent field E then selects the final value from the already-fetched LUT row

panels.label: (f) single-input VLP
panels.differs: implements the split with TCs: numbered phases 1-4 (field split, value reuse, mantissa subscription, exponent subscription) for one input

panels.label: (g) single-input timing
panels.differs: cycle-by-cycle timeline for (f): which LUT row is active each cycle and when the mantissa/exponent subscriptions fire for i:E=2

panels.label: (h) multi-input VLP
panels.differs: replicates (f) across parallel inputs i[0], i[1], i[k], reusing one LUT row's values across inputs that share the same S-M

panels.label: (i) multi-input timing
panels.differs: cycle-by-cycle timeline for (h): three lanes subscribe to their own (sometimes shared) LUT rows at their own cycles

steps.what: input field split: the floating-point input i is split into its sign-mantissa (S-M) and exponent (E) fields
value reuse: the LUT's row output is shared by every input that needs that same row
mantissa temporal subscription: a TC keyed on S-M emits a spike that selects/fetches the correct row from the LUT output stream
exponent temporal subscription: a second TC keyed on E emits a spike that selects the one element within the fetched row

values.what: concrete S-M-E addresses and their exp() outputs (i=2 -> exp(2); S-M=0-3,E=2 -> exp(0-3-2); S-M=0-1,E=1 -> exp(0-1-1)) used throughout to ground the addressing scheme
values.linked_by: colour: red marks the S-M=0-3 row and its values, blue marks the S-M=0-1 row, consistent from the LUT row through the cycle timeline to the final exp output
values.result_cells: each result is a small hexagon labelled with its S-M-E address next to a boxed 'exp(...)' value

content.key_idea: Computing exp() from a LUT is split into two temporal subscriptions: the mantissa selects which row of consecutive values to fetch (shared across inputs needing that row), and the exponent then picks the value from that row.
content.reading_order: Left column (a)-(e) build the row-then-element LUT split conceptually; right column (f)-(i) realize it with TCs, alternating a circuit panel with its cycle-timing diagram, single-input then multi-input.

summary: Figure 3 develops VLP's approximation of a nonlinear function (exp) from a plain lookup table into a pipelined temporal circuit. (a)-(b) show a conventional LUT: one address returns one value, and it can serve only one input at a time. (c)-(e) redesign the addressing as two steps: first fetch a row of consecutive values, then select one; applied to a floating-point input split into sign-mantissa (S-M, addresses the row) and exponent (E, picks the element), this yields exp(S-M-E). (f) implements this for one input with four numbered phases: split the input into S-M/E, reuse the LUT's row output, subscribe to the row via a mantissa-keyed spike, then subscribe to one element via an exponent-keyed spike; (g) shows the matching cycle-by-cycle timing. (h)-(i) replicate the same circuit and timing across parallel inputs, sharing one fetched row whenever inputs share the same S-M.
summary_zh: 图3将exp()查表逐步优化为流水线电路：朴素LUT一次仅服一个输入；改为先取一行再选元素的两步寻址，行由尾数定位、指数选元素；单输入VLP按拆分、复用、尾数订阅、指数订阅四阶段实现，并给出周期时序；再复制到多路输入，共享同一行。
notes: Corrected worked_example from prior False to True (concrete S-M-E addresses and exp values are reused throughout as the running illustration, as in Figure 2's marker). Corrected base from prior 'circuit' (not in this schema's enum) to 'mixed' (LUT tables + circuit blocks + cycle timelines). Confidence set to medium because panels (g) and (i), the cycle-by-cycle timing diagrams, are not walked through in the paper text (only the caption's phase list and paragraph on (a)-(f) are); their exact pipeline-latency semantics (why hexagons appear to shift cycles between the LUT-row track and the per-lane tracks) are inferred from the visual layout, not confirmed by prose.
